title: Ka ʻimi hale
description: Ten short stories about finding and making a home in Hawaiʻi: a house hunt online, a cannonball in the garden, a residents' vote on paint, moving day with a baby, rewiring an old house, a family homestead, the royal mausoleum next door, a pilot's move from the desert, a housewarming feast and a Hawaiian class at the community centre.

lessons.title: Ka hale ma ka pūnaewele
lessons.summary: Puakea and her fiancé Kekauoha look for a rented house in Kāneʻohe on websites, set a limit for the rent, find that the first house by the sea has doubled in price, and write to the owner of a vacant house further inland.
lessons.text:
Ua hoʻopalau ʻo Puakea lāua ʻo Kekauoha i ka mahina ʻo Malaki. E male ana lāua i ka makahiki aʻe, a makemake lāua e loaʻa iā lāua kekahi hale ma mua o ka male ʻana. ʻO ko lāua moeʻuhane, he hale liʻiliʻi kokoke i ke kai, me kekahi māla a me kekahi lumi no nā keiki ma hope aku.

I kēlā me kēia ahiahi, noho lāua ma ka pākaukau a nānā i nā kahuapaʻa o nā hale hoʻolimalima. Aia ma kekahi kahuapaʻa nā hale hakahaka a pau o Kāneʻohe. Kaomi ʻo Puakea i kekahi loulou, a wehe ʻia kekahi ʻaoʻao hou me nā kiʻi o ka hale. Kaomi hou ʻo ia i kekahi loulou ʻē aʻe, a ʻike ʻia nā kiʻi o kekahi hale hou.

Ua hoʻoholo lāua i kekahi kaupalena no ka uku: ʻaʻole e ʻoi aku ka uku o ka mahina ma mua o $2,500. Ma ke kahuapaʻa, hiki ke kaomi i kekahi pihi a hōʻike ʻia nā hale ma lalo o ke kaupalena wale nō.

ʻO ka hale mua, he hale nani ma kekahi kaiahome makai o ke alanui nui. He 60 mika kuea ka nui. Akā ua pālua ka uku o ka mahina ma hope o hoʻokahi makahiki wale nō: he $5,000 i kēia manawa. "Ua pālua ka uku! Ua ʻoi loa aku ia ma mua o ko kāua kaupalena," wahi a Kekauoha.

ʻO ka hale ʻelua, he hale hakahaka ma kekahi kaiahome mālie ma uka. He 80 mika kuea ka nui, ʻekolu lumi moe, a he māla liʻiliʻi. He $2,400 ka uku o ka mahina, ma lalo iho o ko lāua kaupalena. ʻAʻole ia makai o ke alanui, akā hiki ke ʻike ʻia ke kai mai ka puka aniani. Ua kaomi ʻo Kekauoha i ka loulou "E kelepona mai", a ua kākau ʻo ia i kekahi leka i ka mea nona ka hale.

Ke ʻae mai ka mea nona ka hale, e hele ana lāua e nānā i ka hale i ka Pōʻaono. "Aia paha ko kāua moeʻuhane ma kēlā hale," wahi a Puakea.

Nā nīnau:
I ka mahina hea i hoʻopalau ai ʻo Puakea lāua ʻo Kekauoha?
Ua hoʻopalau lāua i ka mahina ʻo Malaki.
He aha ko lāua kaupalena no ka uku o ka mahina?
ʻO $2,500 ko lāua kaupalena.
No ke aha ʻaʻole lāua i koho i ka hale makai?
No ka mea, ua pālua kona uku, a ua ʻoi aku ia ma mua o ko lāua kaupalena.
He aha ka nui o ka hale hakahaka ma uka?
He 80 mika kuea ka nui o ia hale.
Ua kaomi ʻo Kekauoha i ka loulou hea?
Ua kaomi ʻo ia i ka loulou "E kelepona mai".

lessons.title: Ka pōkā ma ka māla
lessons.summary: Kamakoa and his daughter Keonaona dig mounds in the lumpy soil behind their old house in Kapaʻa, pry up a stone and find an old iron cannonball, then plant seeds, an orange tree, roses and ʻilima, and hear the frogs at night.
lessons.text:
Ua neʻe ʻo Kamakoa lāua ʻo kāna kaikamahine ʻo Keonaona i kekahi hale kahiko ma Kapaʻa. Ma hope o ka hale, aia kekahi pā nui. Puʻupuʻu ka lepo o ka pā, a nui nā ʻiliʻili a me nā pōhaku. Makemake ʻo Kamakoa e kanu i nā mea kanu, no laila ua hoʻoholo ʻo ia e hana i nā puʻe lepo.

ʻOiai ʻo Kamakoa e ʻeli ana i nā puʻe, ua ʻohi ʻo Keonaona i nā ʻiliʻili a waiho ʻo ia ia mau ʻiliʻili ma kekahi ʻaoʻao o ka pā. "He nui loa nā ʻiliʻili!" wahi āna. "A puʻupuʻu ka lepo ma nā wahi a pau."

Ma waena o ka pā, aia kekahi pōhaku nui. Ua une ʻo Kamakoa i ka pōhaku me kekahi lāʻau lōʻihi. Ua une hou ʻo ia, a ua neʻe ka pōhaku. Ma lalo o ka pōhaku, ua ʻike ʻo ia i kekahi mea hao poepoe a kaumaha. "He pōkā kahiko kēia!" wahi a Kamakoa.

Ua kelepona ʻo ia i ka hale hōʻikeʻike o Kauaʻi. Ua hele mai kekahi wahine o ka hale hōʻikeʻike a nānā i ka pōkā. "He pōkā ia no kekahi moku kaua o nā makahiki 1800," wahi āna. Ua lawe ʻo ia i ka pōkā i ka hale hōʻikeʻike, i ʻike ka lehulehu i ka pōkā.

A laila, ua hoʻomau lāua i ka hana. Ua kanu ʻo Keonaona i nā ʻanoʻano ma luna o nā puʻe. Ua kanu ʻo Kamakoa i kekahi kumu ʻalani ma ke kihi o ka pā. "Ke ulu ke kumu ʻalani, e ʻai ana kāua i nā ʻalani," wahi āna. Ma ke alo o ka hale, ua kanu lāua i nā loke ʻulaʻula a me nā ʻilima melemele. ʻO ka ʻilima ka pua o Oʻahu, akā nani nō ka ʻilima ma Kauaʻi.

I ke ahiahi, ua ua nui. Ua lohe lāua i nā poloka e kani ana ma ka wai ma lalo o nā puʻe. "Hauʻoli nā poloka i ka māla hou," wahi a Keonaona. Ma hope o ʻelua pule, ua ulu nā ʻanoʻano, a ua pua nā loke a me nā ʻilima.

Nā nīnau:
Pehea ka lepo o ka pā?
Puʻupuʻu ka lepo, a nui nā ʻiliʻili a me nā pōhaku.
He aha ka mea i ʻike ʻia e Kamakoa ma lalo o ka pōhaku?
Ua ʻike ʻo ia i kekahi pōkā hao kahiko.
Ua une ʻo Kamakoa i ka pōhaku me ka aha?
Ua une ʻo ia i ka pōhaku me kekahi lāʻau lōʻihi.
Ua kanu ʻo Keonaona i nā ʻanoʻano ma hea?
Ua kanu ʻo ia i nā ʻanoʻano ma luna o nā puʻe.
He aha ka mea i lohe ʻia e lāua i ke ahiahi?
Ua lohe lāua i nā poloka e kani ana.

lessons.title: Ke koho pāloka
lessons.summary: When an unknown offender paints ugly marks on the wall of their building in Makiki, the residents' association led by Kaʻulu votes by ballot on a new colour; despite a scornful remark, purple wins seventeen to thirteen.
lessons.text:
Noho he 30 ʻohana ma kekahi hale nui ma Makiki. I kekahi pō, ua pena kekahi lawehala i nā kiʻi ʻino ma ka paia ma ke alo o ka hale. I ke kakahiaka, ua ʻike ka poʻe o ka hale i ka paia, a ua huhū lākou. Ua hoʻāhewa kekahi i nā keiki ʻōpio o ke alanui. "Mai hoʻāhewa i nā keiki," wahi a Kealiʻiwahine, he kupuna wahine. "ʻAʻole kākou i ʻike ʻo wai ka lawehala."

Ua kāhea ʻo Kaʻulu, ka pelekikena o ka ʻahahui o ka hale, i kekahi hālāwai. Ua hoʻākāka ʻo ia: "E pena hou ana kākou i nā paia a pau o ka hale. Akā, he aha ka waihoʻoluʻu hou? E koho pāloka kākou." Ua hoʻākāka ʻo ia, ʻelua waihoʻoluʻu wale nō ma ka pāloka: ʻo ka polū a me ka poni.

Ua hoʻowahāwahā kekahi kanaka i ka poni. "He waihoʻoluʻu ka poni no nā keiki liʻiliʻi wale nō," wahi āna. Ua hōʻeuʻeu kēlā ʻōlelo i ka poʻe makemake i ka poni, a ua kamaʻilio nui lākou. A laila, ua kū ʻo Kealiʻiwahine. "Mai hoʻowahāwahā i ka poni," wahi āna. "He waihoʻoluʻu aliʻi ka poni. Ma ka wā kahiko, ua ʻaʻahu nā aliʻi o nā ʻāina he nui i ka poni." Ua hōʻeuʻeu kāna ʻōlelo i nā kānaka he nui.

Ua kākau kēlā me kēia ʻohana i kona koho ma kekahi pāloka, a ua waiho i ka pāloka i loko o kekahi pahu. Ua helu ʻo Kaʻulu i nā pāloka: ʻumikūmāhiku pāloka no ka poni, a he 13 pāloka no ka polū. No laila, ua hoʻāpono ka ʻahahui i ka poni.

Ua hoʻāpono pū ka ʻahahui i kekahi kālā no nā kukui hou ma ke alo o ka hale. Ke hele hou mai ka lawehala i ka pō, e ʻike ʻia ana ʻo ia. Ma ka pukana hou o ka nūpepa liʻiliʻi o ka hale, ua kākau ʻo Kaʻulu i ka hopena o ke koho pāloka. Ua heluhelu nā ʻohana a pau i kēlā pukana. I ka mahina aʻe, ua pena ʻia ka hale i ka poni, a ua pena ʻia nā puka i ka polū.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana a ka lawehala?
Ua pena ʻo ia i nā kiʻi ʻino ma ka paia o ka hale.
He aha nā waihoʻoluʻu ʻelua ma ka pāloka?
ʻO ka polū a me ka poni.
ʻEhia pāloka no ka poni?
He ʻumikūmāhiku pāloka no ka poni.
He aha ka mea i hoʻāpono ʻia e ka ʻahahui?
Ua hoʻāpono ka ʻahahui i ka poni a me ke kālā no nā kukui hou.
Ma hea i kākau ai ʻo Kaʻulu i ka hopena o ke koho pāloka?
Ma ka pukana hou o ka nūpepa liʻiliʻi o ka hale.

lessons.title: Ka lā hoʻoneʻe
lessons.summary: On moving day Hōkūlani and Kapahu drive from Mililani to Hauʻula with their baby; a box on the wheeled board bumps the door and tips over, the traffic crawls, the baby's furry toy walrus goes missing and turns up under the car seat.
lessons.text:
ʻO kēia ka lā hoʻoneʻe o Hōkūlani lāua ʻo kāna kāne ʻo Kapahu. E neʻe ana lāua me kā lāua pēpē ʻo Kauilakea mai Mililani a i Hauʻula, ma kahakai.

I ke kakahiaka nui, ua hoʻopiha lāua i nā pahu he nui. Ua hoʻokomo ʻo Hōkūlani i nā mea pāʻani a ka pēpē i loko o kekahi ʻeke nui: he pea pūhuluhulu, he ʻelepani pūhuluhulu, a me kekahi waleluka pūhuluhulu me ʻelua niho keʻokeʻo lōʻihi. ʻO ka waleluka ka mea pāʻani punahele a ka pēpē. Moe ka pēpē me ka waleluka i kēlā me kēia pō.

Ua lawe ʻo Kapahu i nā pahu i ke kaʻa ma luna o kekahi papa me ʻehā huila. Kaumaha nā pahu, akā maʻalahi ka hana me nā huila. I ka wā i hoʻokuʻi ai ka papa i ka puka, ua kāhuli kekahi pahu, a ua hāʻule nā kīʻaha i ka papahele. Ua hāʻule pū ka ʻeke o nā mea pāʻani. "Mai hoʻokuʻi hou i ka puka!" wahi a Hōkūlani me ka ʻakaʻaka. Ua ʻohi lāua i nā mea a pau a hoʻokomo hou i loko o ke kaʻa.

Ma ke alanui, neʻeneʻe nā kaʻa a pau. Ua neʻeneʻe lākou no ʻelua hola. ʻAʻole hauʻoli ka pēpē. Ua ʻimi ʻo Hōkūlani i ka waleluka i loko o ka ʻeke. Aia ka pea, aia ka ʻelepani, akā ua nalo ka waleluka! "Ua nalo ka waleluka," wahi āna. "Ua hāʻule paha ia i ka wā i kāhuli ai ka pahu."

Ma Hauʻula, ua wehe lākou i ka puka o ke kaʻa. Ua nānā ʻo Kapahu ma lalo o kekahi noho, a aia ka waleluka pūhuluhulu ma laila! Ua hāʻule ka waleluka mai ka ʻeke i ka wā i hoʻokomo hou ai lāua i nā mea i loko o ke kaʻa. Ua hāʻawi ʻo Kapahu i ka waleluka i ka pēpē, a ua ʻakaʻaka ka pēpē. Ia pō, ua moe ka pēpē me ka waleluka ma ka hale hou.

Nā nīnau:
He aha nā mea pāʻani i loko o ka ʻeke?
He pea pūhuluhulu, he ʻelepani pūhuluhulu a me kekahi waleluka pūhuluhulu.
ʻEhia huila ma ka papa?
ʻEhā huila ma ka papa.
He aha ka mea i hana ʻia i ka wā i hoʻokuʻi ai ka papa i ka puka?
Ua kāhuli kekahi pahu, a ua hāʻule nā kīʻaha i ka papahele.
Pehea nā kaʻa ma ke alanui?
Neʻeneʻe nā kaʻa a pau ma ke alanui.
Aia ka waleluka i hea?
Aia ka waleluka ma lalo o kekahi noho o ke kaʻa.

lessons.title: Nā uea kahiko
lessons.summary: Kaimilani asks her brother Kahikina, an electrician, to check the old wires of her house in Waiʻanae; he finds a burnt wire, switches off the power, and when the ladder slips at the edge of the roof he hurts his chest, so she halts the work until he is well.
lessons.text:
Ua kūʻai ʻo Kaimilani i kekahi hale kahiko ma Waiʻanae. Kahiko loa nā uea uila o ka hale, no laila ua kelepona ʻo ia i kona kaikunāne ʻo Kahikina. He kanaka hana uila ʻo Kahikina, a ʻike nui ʻo ia i nā uea.

Ma ka Pōʻaono, ua hele mai kona kaikunāne. Ua wehe ʻo ia i kekahi ʻāpana o ka paia a nānā i nā uea. "E nānā," wahi āna. "Ua ʻā kēia uea i kekahi manawa. ʻEleʻele kona ʻili. Inā ʻaʻole kāua e hoʻololi i nā uea kahiko, e ʻā ana paha ka hale." Ma mua o ka hana ʻana, ua hoʻopio ʻo Kahikina i ka uila o ka hale a pau. "E hoʻopio mau i ka uila ma mua o ka hana ʻana me nā uea," wahi āna i kona kaikuahine.

Ua hoʻokomo ʻo ia i nā uea hou ma loko o nā paia. A laila, ua piʻi ʻo ia i luna o ka hale e hoʻokomo i kekahi uea hou no ke kukui ma waho. Ua hele ʻo ia a kokoke i ka lihi o ka hale. "Mai hele kokoke loa i ka lihi!" wahi a Kaimilani.

Ia manawa nō, ua hiki mai ka ulia. I kona iho ʻana ma ke alapiʻi, ua neʻe ke alapiʻi, a ua hāʻule ʻo Kahikina mai ka lihi o ka hale i luna o ka lepo. Ua hōʻeha ʻo ia i kona umauma. Piha kona lauoho i ka lepo. "Huʻi koʻu umauma," wahi āna.

Ua hoʻokū ʻo Kaimilani i ka hana. "Ua lawa ka hana no kēia lā," wahi āna. Ua lawe ʻo Kaimilani iā ia i ke kauka. Ua nānā ke kauka i kona umauma. "ʻAʻohe iwi i haʻi," wahi a ke kauka. "Ua hōʻeha ʻia kou umauma, akā e pau ana ka huʻi ma hope o hoʻokahi pule." Ma ka hale, ua holoi ʻo Kahikina i ka lepo mai kona lauoho. "Ke pau ka huʻi, e hoʻi hou mai au," wahi āna. "Mahalo, e kuʻu kaikunāne," wahi a Kaimilani.

Nā nīnau:
No ke aha i kelepona ai ʻo Kaimilani i kona kaikunāne?
No ka mea, kahiko loa nā uea uila o kona hale.
He aha ka hana a Kahikina ma mua o ka hana ʻana me nā uea?
Ua hoʻopio ʻo ia i ka uila o ka hale a pau.
Pehea i hiki mai ai ka ulia?
Ua neʻe ke alapiʻi, a ua hāʻule ʻo ia mai ka lihi o ka hale.
He aha ka mea i hōʻeha ʻia?
Ua hōʻeha ʻia kona umauma.
Ua hoʻokū ʻo wai i ka hana?
Ua hoʻokū ʻo Kaimilani i ka hana.

lessons.title: Ka ʻāina o ke kupuna
lessons.summary: In Nānākuli, Kuʻulani's grandfather Kahalewai, now weak, tells how commoners were mistreated and lost their land, how he proved his genealogy and waited thirty years for his homestead, how the families settled the dry land, and his motto to stand firm; Kuʻulani signs up for land of her own.
lessons.text:
Noho ʻo Kuʻulani me kona kupuna kāne ʻo Kahalewai ma kekahi hale ma Nānākuli. He 85 makahiki ko Kahalewai, a palupalu ʻo ia i kēia manawa. Palupalu kona mau wāwae, akā ikaika nō kona manaʻo. I kekahi ahiahi, ua nīnau ʻo Kuʻulani iā ia, "Pehea i loaʻa ai kēia ʻāina iā ʻoe?"

"I ka wā kahiko, ua hoʻomāinoino ʻia nā makaʻāinana," wahi a Kahalewai. "Ua lilo ka ʻāina i nā haole waiwai, a ʻaʻohe ʻāina i koe no nā makaʻāinana he nui. No laila, ua kākoʻo ke aliʻi ʻo Kūhiō i kekahi kānāwai hou i ka makahiki 1921. Ma muli o ia kānāwai, ua hāʻawi ʻia kekahi mau ʻāina i nā kānaka Hawaiʻi."

"I ka makahiki 1960, ua kākau au i koʻu inoa ma ka papa inoa. Pono iaʻu e hōʻike i koʻu kūʻauhau: ka inoa o koʻu makuakāne, o koʻu kupuna kāne, a pēlā aku. Ua hōʻike au i koʻu kūʻauhau, a laila ua kali au. Ua kali au no kanakolu makahiki. Ma hope o kanakolu makahiki, ua loaʻa iaʻu kēia ʻāina."

"I kēlā manawa, he ʻāina maloʻo kēia, ʻaʻohe hale. Ua hoʻopanalāʻau mākou, he 20 ʻohana, i ka ʻāina. Ua kūkulu mākou i nā hale, a ua kanu mākou i nā lāʻau. ʻAʻole maʻalahi ka hoʻopanalāʻau ʻana i ka ʻāina maloʻo, akā ʻaʻohe mea i hoʻomāinoino iā mākou ma ko mākou ʻāina ponoʻī. Ua ulu kaʻu mau kama ʻehā ma kēia ʻāina, a ua hānau ʻia kā lākou mau kama ma kēia hale."

"He mākia koʻu," wahi a Kahalewai. "ʻO koʻu mākia: E hoʻokūpaʻa, a mai haʻalele. Ua hoʻokūpaʻa au no kanakolu makahiki, a ua loaʻa ka ʻāina. Inā makemake ʻoe i kekahi ʻāina, e hoʻokūpaʻa ʻoe."

I ka pule aʻe, ua kākau ʻo Kuʻulani i kona inoa ma ka papa inoa, a ua hōʻike ʻo ia i kona kūʻauhau. "He kama au na kēia ʻāina," wahi āna. "E hoʻokūpaʻa ana au e like me kuʻu kupuna kāne, a ʻo kona mākia koʻu mākia."

Nā nīnau:
Pehea ʻo Kahalewai i kēia manawa?
Palupalu ʻo ia i kēia manawa, akā ikaika nō kona manaʻo.
He aha ka mea i hōʻike ʻia e Kahalewai ma mua o ke kali ʻana?
Ua hōʻike ʻo ia i kona kūʻauhau.
Ua kali ʻo ia no ʻehia makahiki?
Ua kali ʻo ia no kanakolu makahiki.
ʻEhia kama a Kahalewai i ulu ma ka ʻāina?
Ua ulu kāna mau kama ʻehā ma laila.
He aha ka mākia o Kahalewai?
"E hoʻokūpaʻa, a mai haʻalele."

lessons.title: Ka hale kupapaʻu o nā aliʻi
lessons.summary: Nāmaka, who has just moved to Nuʻuanu, visits the royal mausoleum on a day of remembrance; the caretaker explains where the chiefs' remains lie and why the feather standards stand there, she lowers her voice, spreads a lei on the stone, and watches pigeons spread their wings.
lessons.text:
Ua neʻe ʻo Nāmaka i kekahi hale liʻiliʻi ma Nuʻuanu. I kēlā me kēia kakahiaka, holo ʻo ia ma ke alanui, a ʻike ʻo ia i kekahi pā kiʻekiʻe me nā lāʻau nui ma loko. ʻO ia ka hale kupapaʻu o nā aliʻi. I ka hapa nui o nā lā, paʻa ka puka o ka pā.

I kekahi lā hoʻomanaʻo, ua wehe ʻia ka puka. Ua komo ʻo Nāmaka me nā kānaka he nui. Ua hoʻohaʻahaʻa ʻo ia i kona leo, a ua hoʻohaʻahaʻa nā kānaka a pau i ko lākou leo. Ua hoʻokipa ke kahu o ka wahi iā lākou.

Ua hoʻākāka ke kahu: "Aia nā kupapaʻu o nā aliʻi he nui ma lalo o kēia wahi: kekahi mau mōʻī ma hope o Kamehameha, ʻo Kalākaua, ʻo Liliʻuokalani, a me nā aliʻi ʻē aʻe. ʻAʻole naʻe ke kupapaʻu o Kamehameha, ka mōʻī mua, ma ʻaneʻi. Ua hūnā ʻia kona mau iwi, a ʻaʻohe mea i ʻike i kahi i hūnā ʻia ai."

Ma nā ʻaoʻao o ka puka o ka hale, kū ʻelua kāhili lōʻihi. Ua hana ʻia nā kāhili me nā hulu manu. "No ke aha i kū ai nā kāhili ma ʻaneʻi?" i nīnau ai ʻo Nāmaka. "No ka hoʻohiwahiwa ʻana i nā aliʻi," wahi a ke kahu. "Ma nā wahi a nā aliʻi e hele ai, hele pū nā kāhili. A i kēia lā, hoʻohiwahiwa mākou i nā aliʻi me nā kāhili a me nā mele."

Ua lawe mai ʻo Nāmaka i kekahi lei. Ua pāhola ʻo ia i ka lei ma luna o kekahi pōhaku, a ua pāhola nā kānaka ʻē aʻe i nā lei he nui.

Ma waho o ka hale, aia nā nūnū he nui ma ka lepo. I ka wā i hīmeni ai ka poʻe i kekahi mele, ua pāhola nā nūnū i ko lākou mau ʻēheu a lele lākou i luna o nā lāʻau. Ua nānā ʻo Nāmaka i nā ʻēheu keʻokeʻo o nā nūnū. "Ke wehe hou ʻia ka puka, e hoʻi hou mai ana au," wahi āna.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hale ma loko o ka pā kiʻekiʻe?
ʻO ia ka hale kupapaʻu o nā aliʻi.
Aia ke kupapaʻu o Kamehameha, ka mōʻī mua, ma laila?
ʻAʻole. Ua hūnā ʻia kona mau iwi.
No ke aha i kū ai nā kāhili ma ka puka?
No ka hoʻohiwahiwa ʻana i nā aliʻi.
He aha ka mea a Nāmaka i pāhola ai ma luna o ka pōhaku?
Ua pāhola ʻo ia i kekahi lei.
He aha ka hana a nā nūnū i ka wā i hīmeni ai ka poʻe?
Ua pāhola lākou i ko lākou mau ʻēheu a lele i luna o nā lāʻau.

lessons.title: Ka pailaka a me kāna keiki
lessons.summary: Pilot Kalanikini and his son Kanaʻe move from the desert of Las Vegas, where they went after temperate Seattle, to Kailua; they swim, stroll, fly a kite and tour the island, and at night he tells of the galaxy and the Pleiades cluster seen above the sea.
lessons.text:
He pailaka ʻo Kalanikini no kekahi hui mokulele. Ua noho ʻo ia me kāna keikikāne ʻo Kanaʻe ma Las Vegas no ʻelima makahiki. He panoa ʻo Las Vegas. Wela loa ke anilā i ke kau wela, a kākaʻikahi ka ua. Ma mua o Las Vegas, ua noho lāua ma Seattle. He aniau kemepale ko Seattle: ʻaʻole wela loa, ʻaʻole anu loa, akā ua pinepine. "ʻAʻole au makemake i ka panoa, a ʻaʻole au makemake i ka ua pinepine," wahi a Kanaʻe. "Makemake au i ke kai."

I kēia makahiki, ua neʻe lāua i Kailua. Ma ka mokulele, ua noho ʻo Kanaʻe kokoke i ka puka aniani. Ua nānā ʻo ia i ka panoa ma lalo, a laila i ka ʻilikai uliuli o ka moana. "Pehea kou manaʻo no ka ʻilikai mai luna mai?" i nīnau ai ʻo ia i kona makuakāne. "Nani mau," wahi a ka pailaka.

Ma Kailua, maikaʻi ke anilā i nā lā a pau. ʻAʻole wela loa a ʻaʻole anu loa, e like me ka aniau kemepale, akā ʻoi aku ka mehana. ʻAuʻau lāua i ke kai i kēlā me kēia kakahiaka. Ma hope o ka ʻauʻau ʻana, holoholo lāua ma kahakai. I nā lā makani, hoʻolele lāua i kekahi lupe ma ke one. Hoʻolele ʻo Kalanikini i nā mokulele nui i ka lewa, a hoʻolele ʻo Kanaʻe i ka lupe liʻiliʻi.

I nā lā hoʻomaha, kaʻahele lāua ma ka mokupuni. Ua kaʻahele lāua i ka ʻākau o Oʻahu, a ua holoholo lāua ma nā alanui o nā kauhale liʻiliʻi.

I kekahi pō, ua nānā lāua i nā hōkū ma kahakai. "Ke lele au i ka pō ma luna o ka ʻilikai, ʻike au i ka wiliau hōkū," wahi a Kalanikini. "He wiliau hōkū ko kākou, a he nui nā wiliau hōkū ʻē aʻe ma ka lewa." A laila ua kuhikuhi ʻo ia i kekahi huihui hōkū liʻiliʻi. "ʻO ia ka huihui o Makaliʻi. Ma ka huihui hoʻokahi, aia nā hōkū he nui."

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana a Kalanikini?
He pailaka ʻo ia no kekahi hui mokulele.
Pehea ka aniau o Seattle?
He aniau kemepale ko Seattle.
He aha ka mea a Kanaʻe i ʻike ai mai ka puka aniani?
Ua ʻike ʻo ia i ka panoa a laila i ka ʻilikai uliuli.
He aha kā lāua hana ma hope o ka ʻauʻau ʻana?
Holoholo lāua ma kahakai.
He aha ka inoa o ka huihui hōkū liʻiliʻi?
ʻO ka huihui o Makaliʻi.

lessons.title: Ka ʻahaʻaina no ka hale hou
lessons.summary: Pohai and Kauahi hold a feast for their new house in Waimea; the smell of the food tempts the guests, Pohai's school friend, the singer Iolana, gives them her new album, an aunt gives a hat woven from ʻieʻie fibre, the children dance hula ʻauana and the grandmother's gift is a wooden bowl.
lessons.text:
Ua pau ke kūkulu ʻana i ka hale hou o Pohai lāua ʻo Kauahi ma Waimea. No laila, ua hoʻoholo lāua e hana i kekahi ʻahaʻaina no ko lāua ʻohana a me nā hoaaloha. Ua kono lāua i nā kānaka he 40 i ka ʻahaʻaina.

Mai ke kakahiaka nui, ua kuke ʻo Kauahi i ka puaʻa ma lalo o ka honua. Ma mua o ke ahiahi, ua piha ka pā i ka ʻala o ka puaʻa. Ua hoʻowalewale ka ʻala i nā keiki, a ua hele mai lākou i ka lumi kuke. "Mai hoʻowalewale iā mākou!" wahi a lākou me ka ʻakaʻaka. "Makemake mākou e ʻai!"

Ua hiki mai ʻo Iolana, ka hoaaloha o Pohai mai ke kula mai. He pilialoha lōʻihi ko lāua: ma kahi o 25 makahiki. He puʻukani ʻo Iolana, a ua lawe mai ʻo ia i kāna ʻālapama hou. "Ua paʻi ʻia kēia ʻālapama i ka mahina i hala," wahi āna. "ʻO kēia kaʻu makana no ka hale hou." Ua hāʻawi ʻo ia i ka ʻālapama iā Pohai. "Mahalo i ka pilialoha," wahi a Pohai.

Ua lawe mai ka makuahine o Kauahi i kekahi pāpale. Ua ulana ʻia ka pāpale me nā ahelo o ka ʻieʻie. "Ua ʻohi au i ka ʻieʻie ma uka," wahi āna. "Ua hoʻomākaukau au i nā ahelo, a laila ua ulana au i ka pāpale."

Ma hope o ka ʻai ʻana, ua hīmeni ka puʻukani i nā mele o kāna ʻālapama, a ua hula nā kaikamāhine i ka hula ʻauana. "E hula ʻauana pū ʻoe!" wahi a lākou iā Pohai, a ua hula pū ʻo ia.

Ua lawe mai ke kupuna wahine o Pohai i kekahi ʻumeke lāʻau kahiko. "Hō mai i kēlā ʻumeke," wahi a Pohai. Ua hāʻawi ke kupuna wahine i ka ʻumeke iā ia. "He ʻumeke kēia na koʻu makuahine," wahi āna. "E mālama ʻoe i kēia ʻumeke ma kou hale hou." Ua waiho ʻo Pohai i ka ʻumeke ma ka pākaukau ma waena o ka hale. "Hō mai i ka poi, a e hoʻopiha kākou i ka ʻumeke," wahi a Kauahi.

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia kānaka i kono ʻia i ka ʻahaʻaina?
Ua kono ʻia nā kānaka he 40.
He aha ka mea i hoʻowalewale i nā keiki?
Ua hoʻowalewale ka ʻala o ka puaʻa i nā keiki.
He aha ka makana a ka puʻukani?
ʻO kāna ʻālapama hou ka makana.
Ua ulana ʻia ka pāpale me ka aha?
Ua ulana ʻia me nā ahelo o ka ʻieʻie.
He aha ka makana a ke kupuna wahine?
He ʻumeke lāʻau kahiko kāna makana.

lessons.title: Ka papa ʻōlelo ma ke kaiāulu
lessons.summary: In her diary, Kanoelehua, newly moved from Seattle to Kāneʻohe, writes about her Hawaiian class at the community centre: the teacher's two words for consonants, how the kahakō lengthens a vowel, a story where the characters speak with ihola, the words she forgets, and his advice to be patient and listen.
lessons.text:
Pōʻakolu. Ua neʻe au, ʻo Kanoelehua, mai Seattle a i Kāneʻohe i ka mahina i hala. I kēia ahiahi, ua hele au i ka papa ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi ma ka hale o ke kaiāulu. ʻO Kekahuna ko mākou kumu.

Ua aʻo mai ʻo Kekahuna i nā leokanipū. "He ʻewalu leokanipū ma ka ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi," wahi āna. "ʻEhiku huapalapala a me ka ʻokina. Kapa kekahi poʻe i nā leokanipū he koneka. He ʻelua inoa no ka mea hoʻokahi: ʻo ka leokanipū a me ke koneka." Ua kākau au i nā koneka a pau ma kaʻu puke.

A laila, ua aʻo mai ʻo ia i ke kahakō. "Hoʻolōʻihi ke kahakō i ka leo," wahi āna. "E hoʻolohe me ka pepeiao i ka ʻokoʻa o kala a me kālā. Ma ka huaʻōlelo kālā, hoʻolōʻihi ʻia ka leo." Ua hoʻolohe au me koʻu mau pepeiao, a ua lohe au i ka ʻokoʻa.

Ma hope, ua heluhelu mākou i kekahi moʻolelo kahiko. ʻElua hāmeʻe o ka moʻolelo: he kanaka lawaiʻa a me kekahi manu. "Hele ihola ka lawaiʻa i kahakai," wahi a ka moʻolelo. "Kāhea ihola ka manu i ka lawaiʻa." Ua hoʻākāka ke kumu: "Ma nā moʻolelo kahiko, ʻike pinepine ʻia ka huaʻōlelo ihola ma hope o ka hana a kekahi hāmeʻe. Hele ihola ka hāmeʻe: ua hele ʻo ia, a laila hiki mai kekahi mea hou ma ka moʻolelo."

Ua poina iaʻu nā huaʻōlelo he nui. Ua poina iaʻu ka huaʻōlelo no ka manu, a ua poina hou iaʻu ka inoa o ka lawaiʻa. Ma hope o ka papa, ua nīnau au i ke kumu no kekahi aʻoaʻo. ʻO kāna aʻoaʻo: "E hoʻomanawanui. E hoʻolohe i ka ʻōlelo i kēlā me kēia lā, me ka pepeiao a me ka naʻau. Ke poina kekahi huaʻōlelo iā ʻoe, e heluhelu hou." E hoʻomanawanui ana au, a e hahai ana au i kāna aʻoaʻo.

Nā nīnau:
ʻEhia leokanipū ma ka ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi?
He ʻewalu leokanipū ma ka ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi.
He aha ka inoa ʻē aʻe o ka leokanipū?
ʻO ke koneka kekahi inoa.
He aha ka hana a ke kahakō?
Hoʻolōʻihi ke kahakō i ka leo.
ʻO wai nā hāmeʻe o ka moʻolelo?
He kanaka lawaiʻa a me kekahi manu.
He aha ka aʻoaʻo a ke kumu?
"E hoʻomanawanui. E hoʻolohe i ka ʻōlelo i kēlā me kēia lā."
